directAnswer: Pope St. Paul VI was Giovanni Battista Montini, former archbishop of Milan, who reigned from 21 June 1963 to 6 August 1978. He guided the Second Vatican Council to its close, carried out its liturgical reform, traveled to six continents, lifted the 1054 excommunications with Constantinople, and issued Humanae vitae. He was canonized in 2018.

sections.h2: Giovanni Battista Montini, Servant of the Secretariat of State
paras: Giovanni Battista Montini was born on 26 September 1897 in Concesio, near Brescia, the son of a lawyer and Catholic journalist active in politics. Frail as a youth, he was ordained in 1920 and soon entered the Vatican's diplomatic service. He spent three decades in the Secretariat of State, working closely with Pius XII and serving as substitute, and was also chaplain to Italian Catholic university students.

In 1954 Pius XII named him archbishop of Milan, where he devoted himself to reaching industrial workers and organized a large city mission. John XXIII made him the first cardinal of his pontificate in 1958, and Montini was elected pope in June 1963, taking the name of the Apostle Paul.

Paul VI reconvened the Second Vatican Council and presided over its last three sessions, promulgating its sixteen documents, including the constitutions on the liturgy, on the Church, on divine revelation, and on the Church in the modern world. He closed the council on 8 December 1965.

He then implemented it. He created the Synod of Bishops in 1965, reformed the Roman Curia, and promulgated the revised Roman Missal in 1969, which introduced the form of the Mass now celebrated in parishes, increasingly in the vernacular. He was also the last pope to be crowned with the papal tiara, which he later gave away, and it is now displayed at the Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception in Washington, D.C.

sections.h2: The Pilgrim Pope and the Sister Churches
paras: In January 1964 Paul VI made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land, the first papal journey outside Italy in more than 150 years, and met Ecumenical Patriarch Athenagoras I in Jerusalem. On 7 December 1965 the two simultaneously lifted the mutual excommunications of 1054. In 1967 he visited the patriarch in Istanbul.

He traveled to India, to Colombia, to Uganda, where he honored the Ugandan martyrs he had canonized, and to Asia and Oceania. In October 1965 he addressed the United Nations General Assembly in New York, pleading for an end to war, and celebrated Mass at Yankee Stadium during that visit.

sections.h2: Humanae vitae, Populorum progressio and Evangelii nuntiandi
paras: Paul VI's 1967 encyclical Populorum progressio addressed global development and the duties of wealthy nations toward poorer ones. In July 1968 he issued Humanae vitae, which reaffirmed that each marital act must remain open to the transmission of life and rejected artificial contraception. The encyclical met strong dissent in some quarters, and the pope wrote no further encyclicals afterward.

In 1968 he also proclaimed the Credo of the People of God, and in 1975 he issued the apostolic exhortation Evangelii nuntiandi on evangelization in the modern world, a text frequently cited by his successors.

sections.h2: Death on the Transfiguration and Canonization
paras: Paul VI died at Castel Gandolfo on 6 August 1978, the feast of the Transfiguration. Pope Francis beatified him on 19 October 2014 and canonized him on 14 October 2018, alongside St. Oscar Romero. His optional memorial is kept on May 29, the anniversary of his priestly ordination.

keyFacts: Born Giovanni Battista Montini in Concesio on 26 September 1897
Closed the Second Vatican Council on 8 December 1965
Lifted the 1054 excommunications with Patriarch Athenagoras I (1965)
Issued Populorum progressio (1967) and Humanae vitae (1968)
Canonized by Pope Francis on 14 October 2018; memorial May 29

faqs.question: What did Humanae vitae teach?
faqs.answer: Issued by Paul VI in 1968, Humanae vitae reaffirmed that the unitive and procreative meanings of marriage are inseparable and that artificial contraception is morally wrong, while approving natural methods of spacing births for serious reasons.

faqs.question: Where is Paul VI's papal tiara today?
faqs.answer: Paul VI gave up the tiara after his coronation as a gesture of solidarity with the poor. It was later given to the Catholic Church in the United States and is displayed at the Basilica of the National Shrine of the Immaculate Conception in Washington, D.C.

faqs.question: What happened between Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras?
faqs.answer: They met in Jerusalem in 1964, the first meeting of a pope and an ecumenical patriarch in centuries, and on 7 December 1965 they jointly lifted the mutual excommunications of 1054.
